_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
"The container" is the messages container (".messages-container"), "the button" the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button"), and "the gap" the container's scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop. To "send" a message, fill the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) with it and click the send button ([data-testid="send-button"]). Check every assertion with an eval that has "expect" (or an assert_* or wait_* step): an eval without "expect" asserts nothing. When a step says to record something, do it in one eval without "expect" that stores it in the named window variable, then check that variable. Perform the steps in order. The test seeds a long conversation with ID {{ID}}; to "open the conversation", navigate to /c/{{ID}}, wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s), then wait for the first [data-testid="message"] element to be visible (allow 30s). Auto-pinning does not synchronously read back scrollTop. The page counts the container's scrollTop writes in window.__messagesScrollTopWrites, and in window.__messagesScrollTopReadsAfterWrite every read of its scrollTop in the same task as a write (before the next microtask).
1. Open the conversation.
2. Wait until (window.__messagesScrollTopWrites || 0) > 0 is true.
3. (window.__messagesScrollTopReadsAfterWrite || 0) must be exactly 0.
